    Banking Services Officer @ Allied Bank Limited | MBA, Marketing

    8h •

    PKR 57,182,260,838. That is what Pakistani banks have surrendered to the State Bank in unclaimed deposits between 2015 and 2025.
    Nobody publishes this number. SBP releases one Excel file per bank, per year never a total.

    The average is the whole story. PKR 5,034 is not a rich man's fortune.
    It is a salary account from a job someone left.
    A term deposit a #father opened and never mentioned. And it is spreading, not shrinking.
    Since 2015 the amount grew 2.4x the number of accounts grew 4.6x.
    More people, smaller balances. One caveat I will not bury: this is a floor, not a total.

    The real figure is higher. Next: how to check whether your name is on that list.

    #Banking #Pakistan #StateBankOfPakistan #PersonalFinance #BankingIndustry

              Holy sh*t
              Opus 5.5 could be insane.


              LLM benchmarks never really translated into real performance in agentic coding.
              Opus 5 meeting Fable 5's coding capability in SWE bench did not translate into actually using it at all.

              Cursor bench however, was one benchmark that did somewhat translate well when it comes to cost to performance, which placed opus 5 meaningfully lower and more expensive per task than Fable high effort

              BUT

              Opus 5.5 seems to be a completely new frontier

              You want a model to be on the right (cheaper) and towards the top (agentic coding performance)

              Opus 5.5 is as close to the top right as LLMs have gotten, after being the sheer performance dominator

              Now all thats left is to use it.

                      Sandip Jaiswar

                      • 2nd

                      Frontend Architect & Engineering Mentor | Helping Experienced Developers Move to Senior, Lead & Architect Roles | Angular • React • Architecture | 14+ Years

                      Visit my website

                      10h •

                      A lot of frontend developers are going to feel this late.

                      Not because React or Angular suddenly became useless.

                      But because the role itself is changing.

                      I keep seeing experienced developers saying the same things:

                      “Calls are less.”
                      “Competition is too high.”
                      “Should I learn backend?”
                      “Should I learn AI?”

                      And then they get stuck trying to learn everything.

                      That’s the part I’d be worried about.

                      Not AI itself.

                      Losing another 6–12 months without deciding what your next version should look like.

                      If you’ve been doing frontend for years, maybe the question now is not:

                      “Which framework should I learn next?”

                      Maybe it’s:

                      “What do I need to add so I’m still relevant for the next 5 years?”

                      For some people, that means full stack.
                      For some, AI.
                      For some, both.
